# Billing System Migration Rollout Plan
## 40,000 Users — Old Billing System → New Billing System (Dual-Run Supported)

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 users in three phases, leveraging the ability to run both billing systems concurrently. The old system remains fully operational as a fallback throughout all user-migration phases, and is only scheduled for retirement after 100% of users have been successfully migrated and validated.

---

## Phase 1: Canary (2% of users — 800 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end integration testing in staging, including invoice generation, payment capture, refunds, tax calculation, and dunning workflows against production-mirrored data. On-call rotation and rollback tooling (instant revert to old system per-account) are confirmed working.

**Cohort:** Internal employees, opt-in beta users, and low-risk accounts (no active disputes, standard payment methods, month-to-month plans).

**Duration:** 1–2 weeks minimum, with daily metric review.

**Exit criterion to advance:** All halt-metric thresholds (below) stay green for 7 consecutive days, and support ticket volume for migrated cohort is within 1.5x baseline.

---

## Phase 2: Expansion (25% of users — 10,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full soak period with zero unresolved Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents attributable to the new system, reconciliation between old and new ledgers shows 100% match for the canary cohort, and finance has signed off on billing accuracy for Phase 1 data.

**Cohort:** Broader random sample stratified across plan types, geographies, and payment methods (cards, ACH, invoicing) to surface edge cases before full-scale exposure.

**Duration:** 2–3 weeks, migrated in sub-waves of ~2,500 users every 3–4 days to allow metric observation between waves.

**Exit criterion to advance:** Halt metrics remain green through the full phase; failed-payment rate and support escalation rate stay within agreed tolerance across all sub-waves.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability / Full Migration (73% of users — 29,200 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 fully complete with reconciliation match rate ≥99.99% across all migrated accounts, no open critical defects in the new system, customer support fully trained and staffed for full-volume ticket load, and finance/compliance sign-off obtained for scaling to 100%.

**Cohort:** All remaining users, migrated in weekly waves of roughly 15% of total users (~6,000/week) rather than a single big-bang cutover, prioritizing lower-risk segments first and highest-complexity enterprise/legacy accounts last.

**Duration:** 4–5 weeks.

**Exit criterion:** 100% of the 40,000 users successfully migrated and reconciled; old system placed into a read-only "dual-run cooldown" state for a minimum of one full billing cycle (to catch late invoices, disputes, and refunds) before any decommissioning work begins. Decommissioning of the old billing system is explicitly a **separate, later phase**, not part of Phase 3.

---

## Risks

RISK: Billing discrepancies between old and new systems cause customers to be over- or under-charged | Run parallel ledger reconciliation daily during migration with automated diffing and a finance sign-off gate before each phase advances | Finance Systems Lead
RISK: New system cannot handle peak transaction volume once a large cohort is migrated | Load-test the new system at 2x projected Phase 3 volume before Phase 2 starts, with autoscaling and capacity alerts configured | Platform/Infrastructure Lead
RISK: Migrated customers experience failed or duplicate payment charges during cutover | Freeze billing runs for an account during its migration window and implement idempotency keys on payment capture in the new system | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by a spike in billing-related tickets | Stagger migration waves, pre-train support staff per phase, and stage a rollback runbook they can trigger without engineering escalation | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Data migration errors (missing payment methods, incorrect plan mapping) go undetected until a billing cycle runs | Run pre-migration data validation scripts per account and a post-migration automated audit comparing key fields against the source system | Data Migration Engineer

---

## Halt / Rollback Metrics

Roll back the current wave and pause further migration if, within any 24-hour window post-migration:

- **Payment failure rate for migrated accounts exceeds 2%** (vs. established old-system baseline), OR
- Billing reconciliation mismatch rate exceeds **0.1%** of migrated accounts, OR
- Sev-1 incident count attributable to the new billing system exceeds **0** (i.e., any Sev-1 triggers an automatic pause pending root cause).

Rollback mechanism: affected accounts are flagged back to the old billing system (dual-run makes this a routing-table change, not a data restore), and the responsible on-call lead conducts root-cause review before resuming the phase.

PHASES: 3
